analysis.answer: Under current law, each county has the authority to decide whether its jail will honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure eliminates that local discretion and establishes a statewide rule prohibiting any county jail from holding an individual past their normal release time based solely on a federal immigration detainer.

Federal immigration authorities may adapt by attempting to take custody of individuals before their scheduled release or by securing judicial warrants rather than relying on administrative detainers. Local jails will need to adjust their protocols to ensure individuals are released immediately when their local charges or sentences are resolved.

The measure addresses the concern that holding individuals on administrative immigration detainers deprives them of liberty without a judicial warrant or independent local charges. By prohibiting the practice, the mechanism directly prevents local jails from being used for federal immigration detention. At the same time, it removes a tool used by federal authorities to assume custody of undocumented individuals directly from secure local facilities.

The state government gains power by preempting local policy. Undocumented immigrants gain protection from administrative detention. Federal immigration authorities lose the convenience of having local jails hold individuals on their behalf, and local county sheriffs lose the discretion to cooperate with such detainers.
